title: Second Temple Administration
aliases: Jewish institutions under Persia and Rome
summary: The changing network of temple personnel, high priests, scribes, elders, local assemblies, councils, and imperial authorities that ordered Jewish public life from Persian restoration to 70 CE.
historical_context: Second Temple administration changed substantially across Persian, Hellenistic, Hasmonean, Herodian, and Roman rule. Temple and Torah remained central, but no single arrangement should be projected across the entire 515 BCE-70 CE period.
ancient_near_east_context: Persian provincial administration is relevant to the early period; Hellenistic civic and Roman provincial structures are more relevant later. Comparative institutional claims must be tied to a particular century and source.
hebraic_worldview: Temple holiness, Torah, priestly teaching, sacrifice, purity, communal responsibility, and hope for divine rule shaped institutional life even when offices were entangled with imperial power.
second_temple_context: Ezra-Nehemiah presents early priestly, Levitical, scribal, and gubernatorial arrangements. Josephus, inscriptions, the Gospels, and Acts attest later high priests, temple officers, synagogues, named groups, and councils under Herodian and Roman power.
canonical_context: The institution links restoration texts with the late Second Temple setting of the Gospels and Acts while preserving the centuries of political and social change between them.
literary_context: Ezra-Nehemiah, Malachi, the Gospels, Acts, Josephus, inscriptions, and Qumran texts use different genres and terminology. They should not be flattened into a single constitutional description.
covenantal_significance: These institutions organized worship and communal identity under successive empires, while biblical texts also expose contested legitimacy, corruption, reform, and incomplete restoration.
original_audience: Readers tracing how postexilic temple and Torah institutions developed into the diverse Jewish leadership world of the Gospels and Acts.
historical_setting: Jerusalem, Judea, and Jewish diaspora communities from approximately 515 BCE to 70 CE under successive imperial and local regimes.
canonical_role: This record provides the diachronic institutional overview; detailed evidence and passage ranking belong to the linked Persian, priestly, synagogue, scribal, and sectarian clusters.

interpretive_notes.note: Second Temple administration is a periodized family of institutions rather than one bureaucracy unchanged from Ezra to Caiaphas.
interpretive_notes.rationale: Sources from different centuries attest changing rulers, offices, and jurisdictions.

interpretive_notes.note: Pharisees, Sadducees, scribes, chief priests, and councils overlap in some sources but are not interchangeable labels.
interpretive_notes.rationale: Each term has its own source history and social range.
